description.value: The study investigated grey and white matter correlates of recent and remote autobiographical memory retrieval in behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia, semantic dementia, Alzheimer's disease, and healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry and diffusion tensor imaging.

value: Based on previous studies, we predicted frontal and medial temporal lobe involvement irrespective of epoch.
Integrity of the lateral temporal cortices was predicted to be strongly associated with remote ABM retrieval, suggestive of a crucial role for semantic processing in the retrieval of old memories.
In contrast, we expected that integrity of midline posterior parietal structures, important for self-referential processing and visual imagery, would correlate with the retrieval of recent events.

description.value: Observational cross-sectional study of dementia patients and healthy controls.

spans.text: This study is the first to contrast the neural substrates of recent and remote ABM using a combination of whole-brain voxel-based morphometry analyses and tract-based spatial statistics in neurodegenerative disorders.

value: AD patients showed widespread grey matter intensity decreases relative to Controls, most pronounced on the left, involving medial temporal regions including the amygdala and hippocampus bilaterally, bilateral lateral temporal cortices, and frontal regions including the orbitofrontal cortex and frontal poles bilaterally.
